data: the story is well worth it
Challenging puzzles and a great story, 10/10
Overall great game, amazing graphics and bumfuzzling puzzles
One of the best puzzle games I've ever played, the music is so relaxing, the puzzles are challenging and fun, and the graphics are great
Amazing puzzles/gameplay, amazing story, amazing game
The ending is just the worst

Great puzzles with a possibly even better story. The puzzle mechanics get introduced very naturally through learning by doing, which makes you feel like a genius when figuring out a mechanic that was previously unknown to you. The game is a good in between of not being too easy but having some hard puzzles in the mix with some even harder optional puzzles. Whilst I bought this game for the puzzles the story is what made me want to write this review. The themes of personhood and AI hold up possibly even better today than when this game was made. Genuinely an amazing game.

The Talos Principle plays very similarly to a Portal mod, except with a whole bunch of philosophical pondering about civilization and the legacy of humanity. I think the unfortunate thing is that the puzzles never feel very difficult, and the narrative never had me invested beyond one or two characters. I had such a lack of investment that I was surprised the ending story beats struck me at all, and had me wishing I could feel the rest of the game to the same degree.

I think the primary turn off for me is that The Talos Principle feels like "Unreal Engine: The Game", with assets that feel bought off the Unreal Engine Marketplace. It doesn't help that the environments are some of the most commonly explored places in games: ruins of ancient civilizations such as Rome and Egypt. While these environments are necessary to set up the themes and story of the game, in tandem with the unchallenging puzzles, it just makes me feel as if the game lacks an identity.

A lot of promise in this title, but the execution makes it come out to a middling experience.

I liked this game. The puzzle aspect of the game is well made although sometimes I felt like the difficulty of the puzzles was way higher in some arbitrarily chosen levels throughout the game. I felt like some balancing would be nice. 

Haven't really played any of these philosophy-oriented games but I will say that the story is different from the typical sci-fi technological dystopias even though it might at one point feel like the backstory is similar. 

The story even makes sense when you think about it, which couldn't be said of even "The Matrix". Challenge me on this one. 

While the terminals are completely optional in this game, they are well placed to make you think about the underlying world enough while doing the puzzles so that the next time you open a terminal, you aren't overwhelmed or uninterested. I want to say that the Serpent is "technically correct" in almost all arguments it says, but that it isn't necessarily a good thing. Which this game is all about, after all

10/10. A masterpiece of a puzzle game with a thrilling finale and an amazing soundtrack. My one gripe is the handful of puzzles that rely on precise timing and movements more than logic; I'm here to use my brain power, not to test my middle-aged reflexes. Apart from that, the best game I've ever played. Better than Portal (I said what I said).

I went in expecting a neat little puzzle game similar to Portal, came out questioning my very own existence and the meaning of life...

This game is amazing: Looks beautiful, plays great, soundtrack is so peaceful and relaxing you can listen to it for hours, masterfully designed puzzles that strike almost perfect balance between challenging and frustrating and a philosophical story that mentally challenges you in ways you didn't think was possible for a game.

In short just do me a favor and buy the damn game already or at least on a sale but just do it !

What is soul? What is life? What is there, upon death? Why are we all here? What happens when we leave? How to imagine the world where there's no "me"?

You know I'm really fond of all this "food for thought/brain" stuff so this game couldn't just pass me by, it got right into my heart and made me compassionate for the protagonist, for all the prisoners of Gehenna, for all the messengers, for Milton, for Admin, even for ELOHIM. In this game there were some moments, some parts of the plot when I just stopped playing and spent hours thinking of what I'd just read/heard. And there were moments I thought I would never continue playing it because these ideas from messages were incredibly terrifying for me. All this existential topics I always feared to discuss even with myself were brought from the inside and put right before me. And I had to overcome it again and again. The challenge is much more than one room with a sigil.
It's not just a puzzle game. It's some sort of a school. See -> read -> understand -> percieve -> solve.

The meta aspect of this game is really attractive. For anyone enjoying questioning the nature of consciousness, The Talos Principle is a really good game for it. Other than that, the overall puzzles difficulty is manageable, and for players that always want to be challenged, the stars are sometimes difficult to find.
The soundtrack is soothing and plays nicely with this puzzle game. I found myself playing it quite a few times outside of the game, just loosing myself in my thoughts.

Certainly the most literary of all the puzzle games I've played, and all the more interesting for it. The puzzles are mostly satisfying, but for me the musings on the nature of consciousness and the Greek allegories that tie into the main story remain the most compelling parts.

If you're a fan of the kind puzzles you meet in Portal, you should consider this game.
Interesting puzzles, a nice story, cool lore, ester eggs and secrets, The Talos Principle has it all!

Other reviews saying this game is basicly Portal is correct although this game focus more on large scale world situations and learning the background concepts is interesting and genius. The game also does a great job of having puzzles start out simple and get more complex after you have been well established into it.
The Talos Principle is one of those very few games that can be considered "true" art. The way it blends its storytelling with its environment is phenomenal and advances the medium. Highly recommend.

Do you like Portal? Do you like any puzzler game for that matter? Do you like to have an awesome story to go with it? This is THE game to play my freind, you won't be disappointed. A second one is coming out soon!

The Talos Principle is an amazing experience that mixes logic puzzles and philosophical questions. It features gorgeous levels, a beautiful sountrack, many well-designed puzzles, a lot of secrets to search for, and thoughtful discussion about existence with an AI.
This game will make you think, and sometimes it will play you instead.

Relaxed puzzle solving and some neat new gameplay features.

Being able to "record" yourself and then interact with your recording is quite a difficult concept to get your head around at first. The portal gun is child's play compared to this. (Disclaimer: Portal / Portal 2 are very good games that I enjoyed very much)

Once I've forgotten the solution to most of the puzzles, I will definitely play The Talos Principle again.

This is by far my favourite puzzle game. It provides challenges not only for your puzzle solving skills but also for your mind in general.
I was pleased to see references to mythology, especially the Greek, which I'm a big fan of. Mythological Talos - a mechanical man, made to protect. The hero of this story is a mechanical man of a new era, that protects something in a way too. But what is it? That's what player is going to find out during the course of this journey.
The story is told through computer terminals, that contain pieces of human knowledge from different times and places, audio recordings and messages from the previous adventurers.

On the technical side, I think it's worth to mention that this game has very good options for preventing motion sickness which is really important for me. And the fact that you can choose third-person view instead of first-person one is satisfying.

The most beautiful game I've ever played by far!!!
It has such an overwhelming and immersive atmosphere that I can't even describe it.
The game itself looks astonishing, the worlds are just perfect - the music, the buildings, everything.

If you are hesitating whether to buy it or not, just go for it! You won't regret it!
Try to solve the puzzles without help and choose the ending you fancy the most! :)

Description: A solid puzzle game with a background in philosophy and religion that routinely challenges both but in a limited way resulting from rote defined choices. There is a lot to explore here but beware of early frustration in communication of philosophical perspective. The puzzles, though simple to start, are fun throughout

By a very small margin I would recommend this game to people who like to play these sorts of puzzle-adventure games. It's beautiful, imaginative and, for a while, fun to solve the many clever puzzles. But as the difficulty of the puzzles begins to exceed the more-frustrating-than-fun threshold, the game loses its appeal. I had fewer than ten puzzles (of the original more-than-100) remaining to be solved in order to reach the game's endings when I decided it just wasn't worth the effort to continue.

Super fun puzzle game. The difficulty curve sometimes is a bit weird (eg. level 1 harder than level 7) but I suppose that depends on how each persons brain works. Tons of extra content as well if you're a completionist. If you like wracking your head, this is the game for you. There's also a little bit of 'secret texts' for those willing to go the extra mile.

Nice at first, a burden at the end (with the DLC). Had to use guides. Recommended for players who like challenging puzzles without a real storyline. Time to 100%: ~29h (with guides). Difficulty: 😈😈

My Curator Page

Let's just address the elephant in the room first - yes, this shares many similarities to Portal. That's a good thing.

This is a really enjoyable 3D puzzle game that, very pertinent to our time, explores the concepts of AI and consciousness. It's an enjoyable game for sure and one I recommend. The one thing I'll say is that, unlike Portal 2 in particular, there is a tremendous amount of quiet space. What I mean by that is that the majority of the time it's just music and puzzles. For some, that sounds ideal. For me, I enjoyed the humor and narrative elements sprinkled between activities in Portal 2. That's not to say it doesn't exist, just that it is far more sparse.

I look forward to playing the sequel which I recently purchased as well.

Es un juego que quiebra los estereotipos que tienen las generaciones mayores de que este medio es invariablemente infantil. Es una obra de arte. Los rompecabezas son lo suficientemente desafiantes como para premiar sin frustrar. Ir recomponiendo la trama mediante los fragmentos de texto y audio que están dispersos a través de los niveles es muy grato.

This is a very pleasant game. Initially, the stupid sudoku puzzles turned me away. But then, some time after, I finally decided to finish the game because everyone had good opinion about it, and it didn't disappoint. I eventually got used to solving those stupid sudoku puzzles and even had fun doing so. The landscape is very beautiful in this game, and so is the music. The game is not opinionated at all, in contrast to the politically-obsessed modern games. It just "shows" and "doesn't tell". The player themself are supposed to interpret the visuals or the texts and decide for themselves the meaning of all that. Overall, it was a joyful journey, and the game looks surprisingly good for its age.

This is one of those games that I would recommend that everyone plays because not only is it a very well paced & amazingly creative puzzle game, but because it centers its very good plot around a concept that are very important in modern politics. That being 'What is a person'?
I don't think I would recommend this at full price, but it is a steal when it is 85% -90% off (which it is a lot).
This game is one that I would recommend fully engaging with the story as this will allow you to get something out of the experience. It will have things for you to think about no mater your stance on the matter.
For the puzzles themselves, they are amazing as there are only a few actual mechanics but they are used in many different ways to make so many great puzzles. Also most of the puzzles are on the shorter end of the number of steps required, so the puzzles came down to mostly creative thinking rather than raw computational thinking.
This game is not perfect however, Honestly the stars are not worth it (it does not even get you the good ending). If you are doing the stars I would recommend that you use this hint guide as otherwise it will be super not fun: (especially since some not are actual puzzles, but rather just hiding).
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=354991567

I'm not even gonna explain anything, just play it and you'll understand.

Alright, I'll write something. It's the Witness but 100x better. You can beat the whole game pretty easily but if you want to get everything there is in the game, it's gonna take a long ass time. About 30-40 hours if you include the DLC. The puzzles constantly get harder and more inventive, the story is honestly fun to piece together, and the multiple endings actually make sense.

That doesn't mean the game isn't without its flaws though. For me, the Tetromino puzzles (tetris puzzles) were a huge flaw. They were simple but my idiotic brain thinks the 2d puzzles where you have all the pieces are harder than the 3d ones where you don't. I dunno, they just frustrated me. That, and some of the ways to get the stars is convoluted as hell, needing you to go on a goose chase around 20 different puzzles to get something you could see at the beginning. Some people think that's fun and cool, I just think it's tedious after the 7th time.

Still, great fucking game.

Surprise I never reviewed this game. Played it when they were demoing at PAX South and I believe one of the developers told me it was like Portal 2 which, at the time, I was in love with and arguably still am. Went home and purchased it. Definitely one of the best puzzle games I have ever played. Used guides to get the "true" ending because some of them were difficult as hell haha.

TL;DR Best puzzle game ever made, right by Portal 2.

i really wasn't expecting a puzzle game/portal clone to make me have an existential panic attack. but the more i played it the more i kept sinking into a hole. The writing of this game is like if Asimov took a line of Sartre laced Kant and tried to write paradise lost.

which you might have to google to understand.

some the puzzles were annoying more than they were difficult, but the quality is pretty consistent all the way through. However it does get pretty samey, and i found myself finishing puzzles just to move the story along, which probably isn't good?

i finished this game months ago and still haven't quite recovered.
Talos Principle is a great puzzle game, with an intriguing storyline that touches on what it means to be a person. If you are a fan of the genre you should definitely check it out.

This was a really fun puzzle-based game that forced you to think quite hard about the problems. Also had a weird (and quite heavy-handed) existential story element, but don't worry, you can pretty much ignore it. It's a beautiful looking game, too.
If you liked Portal and Portal2 this is about as close as it's going to get. Multiple endings, multiple solutions, hidden puzzles. Easily 20-80 hours of fun.

One of the greatest puzzle games.
- Fantastic writing that honestly made me stop, think and question myself.
- Great puzzles with good pacing, alternating from big tough ones to shorter ones to take a breather all while also giving plenty of freedom to the players to skip some for a while or play them in different order within a world.
- 10/10 soundtrack, Damjan always delivers godlike stuff.
- Classic croteam easter eggs all over the place too. :)
- Frogs are people too

My only minor complaint: Some secret stars are way too obtuse to find and not hidden in a "smart puzzle" way but just physically hidden in a way that will make you spin in circles for hours unless you look at an online solution.

"The Talos Principle" is one of those games that draws you in fast and won't easily let go.
While there is a lot of text to go through to get every part of the overarching story it is all well worth it. The puzzles in this game are just as mind-boggling as the philosophical principles strewn throughout the game, and it is addicting.
If you love puzzle games that actually make you think, buy this game.
Tremendously deeply philosophical story about conscience, being a human and artificial intelligence, and great puzzles
It was so good, I don't even know what to say. You should experience it for yourself. Maybe wait for a sale tho.

this is a good game you should definitely try if you like puzzle games, none of the puzzles are too hard to understand and it spends a lot of time teaching the mechanics to you. oh yeah its also a really fun game to speedrun
The gameplay is puzzles, some quite challenging, but just puzzles. But the setting, the philosophical dialog, mini stories and everything is just wonderful.
This game can be summarized in one word: masterpiece. It's one of the best gaming experiences I've ever had. The puzzles are fun, the graphics awesome and the story deep.

The puzzles start off simple and then get much more difficult. Even the more difficult puzzles, however, can be beaten with enough persistence. it maintains a good balance that puzzle games require: a challenge without losing its player's interest. If you have been looking for a game that calls for you to slow down, think, and appreciate the complexity of a created world, then pick up the Talos Principle. the price might be a bit high for an indie game but it has lots of content to offer and it gets a good discount when its on sale.

Its a truly excellent, to put it lightly and the puzzles are fantastic, with stoic philosophy wrapped into it. Definitely makes it worth a buy/try, even if puzzle games are not your thing. You may not know it yet, after many years of ownership or maybe very quickly, it doesn't matter how long, in reality. I think there is massive value in this game and the devs have done a exemplary job. Just buy it on sale if your really not sure, otherwise, just give it a go.

One of the best - if not the best - puzzle games ever made. Everything is perfect, whether the environment, sound design, music, voices and level-design. Difficulty curve is absolutely on point and deserves a bit of explanation : puzzles in Talos Principle require accessories (like cubes f.e). Each accessory is used separately before being integrated in a puzzle with some others. More accessories bring more diversity and therefore more difficulty.
The plot is really nice and all endings are worth viewing. Also, the DLC is definitely worth buying.
In 2 words : Fantastic game.

A masterclass of puzzle design, which, although not quite as airtight as Portal's, allows for more flexibility. Essentially, this game is everything that the Witness tried to be.

4/5

One of the best games that I recently played. I can recommend this game to anyone that likes logical games with a great (but somewhat hidden) background story.

When I started to play this game it was like: eee... another puzzle game, no big deal. But after few levels I realized that I need to know what happened, why this world was created and what is the purpose of it. And finally when I finished the game with "the proper ending" everything "clicked".

Cons:
* some puzzles could be harder
* after playing a while you realize that most of the levels are based on the same schematic
* some of the textures and models look like taken from serious sam (*)
* no co-op multiplayer ;)

Pros:
* great background story
* great music
* great graphics
* great humor
* a lot of additional materials hidden in the game
* some puzzles are challenging (specially the "extras")
* combining multiple level chambers to get the "extra" items
* mechanics (specially the "replay")
* references to sersious sam ;)
* easter eggs

*) Actually if you get deep into the lore of the game it is not directly explained why, but still in my opinion it was a cheap cheat by the developers.
truly excellent. one of the best puzzle games I have ever played. on par with portal

If you loved the portal series, you're sure to enjoy this one ! Plenty of puzzles, some are easy, some really make you think out of the box. Relaxing ambient music plays while you solve puzzles. And finally the game really makes you question existence, consciousness, the soul, AI and the moral ramifications of your interactions with the world around you in RL. 10/10
I love this game! It's chill, and the ambiance is great. The plot is prety good, too - minimal, and only caught in snippets, but it is thought provoking and generally rounds out the whole setting.

Puzzles, puzzles, and more puzzles. It can get a little tedious, but just about the time you get sick of doing puzzles you start caring about the story enough to keep you going. The challenges were not too difficult, but still made you think. The odd one really took some time to solve, but I'm no expert at puzzle games. (I could only get about 10 minutes into Myst.) Overall, it's a good game and worth the money.

One of the most chill and comfy puzzles games I've played. The DLC story was more enjoyable than the base game, but it's intertwined with the base game story. 

The standard puzzles were easy to moderate, while I avoided the star puzzles entirely. Very fun game.

✔ Excellent graphics engine, very competent and offers very good performance
✔ Mesmerizing environments, splendid artistic choices
✔ Excellent level and puzzle design
✔ Great soundtracks, very fitting
✔ Great writing, multiple branches/choices and endings, great story overall
✔ Very good control scheme, feels tight and responsive
✔ A lot of secrets and out-of-bounds things to discover
✔ Super polished production overall
✔ GNU/Linux support!

✘ Textures tend to unload/load too frequently and are too noticable, but it can be forgiven given the theme of the game.

Highly... highly... HIGHLY recommended.

I try not to abuse these words, but Talos Principle is one of the coziest, comfiest games on steam. You spend time in peaceful, abandoned ruins solving the puzzles you want to solve, when you want to solve them. Finding the secrets you want to find, when you want to find them. Reading the backstory you want to read, when you want to read it. The game never gets up in your face with forced cutscenes or set pieces--Its just you and the puzzles, no bullshit.

For once, I'm excited to see what non-serious Sam project Croteam thinks up next.

A very captivating premise delivered through an island of puzzles. While these puzzles were a bit too difficult/frustrating for me at times, I thought the world and it's secrets were the perfect reward to keep exploring and unravelling the mysteries of the game. I really enjoyed the audio logs, the philosopical text, the ending, and the overall narrative. The puzzles were good enough, but my enjoyment of them was really a means to and end....and what an end it was!

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (96%): players love the story and characters, and many praise the challenging puzzles.
The main complaint is the ending, which only a small share of reviews criticize.

details.text: Reviews from the last month are a little less positive than the all-time score, at 93%, a small dip.
New players are far less positive, at 72% within their first 2 hours, than long-time players.
